body:
Thalanbor the Boundless Artwright’s Library is a named library in Fein Uaill. The artwright’s name gives it a place in the history of creation; the surviving visits give it readers, difficult books, poetry and arguments about what knowledge is for.

A visual and a name

The location directory and supplied moving record establish a monumental scholarly place in Fein Uaill. Its full name associates it with Thalanbor the Boundless Artwright, whose surviving testament describes a lifetime spent studying creation. The library’s name does not establish whether he founded, designed, owned or endowed it.

A place of continuing study

On 4, Month of Hope, Year 2, Eldin enters and chooses a book called Songs of Grundy. He reads a poem aloud, trying to find its rhythm. Magnus arrives with a dusty tome, surprised and pleased to find him there. The scene begins with two readers enjoying the same space before their questions become a conversation.

Magnus seeks knowledge of life and artifice because he thinks a figure of Thalanbor’s reputation might have investigated them. That is Magnus’s hope, rather than proof that the artwright created life. Eldin says that he enjoys learning things he had not known existed. He also says that the company worked hard to find this place and that he has been returning between periods of rest.

Books that do not give up their answers easily

Adelia joins the readers and searches older shelves. She finds a small locked book, brings it to the table and tries to open it. Its contents remain unknown. The others speculate and suggest help, but the scene does not turn that volume into an identified treasure or into Thalanbor’s sacred tome.

The research also demands more than enthusiasm. Eldin encourages Magnus, and Adelia later lends guidance, yet Magnus ends one attempt frustrated that the library’s secrets still elude him. He tries another volume embroidered with a golden anvil and hammer; that decoration is not an identification of its author. Tea and company continue beside the work.

A legacy with more than one place of study

The company’s successful recovery of Thalanbor’s craftlore precedes these visits. On 25–26, Month of the Wyrm, six researchers bring several documents together in an unnamed library favored by the Silver Star in Zarathis. The narrator confirms success and directs them to the artwright’s testament. The scene supplies a full account of how the company came to understand his work.

That earlier library has its own evidence. No statement names it as this one. The later library scenes likewise do not locate Thalanbor’s forge hammer, chisel or sacred tome here.

Read the full recovery story → · Explore Thalanbor’s legendary crafting paths →

Learning how to use knowledge

Magnus returns on 5, Month of Hope with new hopes for the books. Eldin is there again, and their conversation moves between research and what it means to lead Zarathis. Eldin urges him to understand the factions’ different strengths and inspire people rather than try to direct every choice. Magnus accepts some of the criticism while continuing to argue for innovation.

The exchange gives the library an intellectual life beyond the search for a powerful object. People read, disagree and reconsider what they should do with their knowledge. On 17, Month of Aionia, Year 3, they are studying there again. Magnus hopes to learn about the gods’ origins, while both men acknowledge that this collection may not hold what he needs. A question brought into the library is not always a question the library answers.

The open record

The library’s foundation date, administration, complete collections and admission rules remain unresolved. Its readers establish continuing use, not the present location of its namesake. Nor do their later investigations grant Thalanbor credit for creating life, artificial soldiers or a complete history of the gods.
